versions.short: The bill would allow certain public libraries, including those run as nonprofit, charitable, or trust organizations, to act as passport acceptance facilities and keep the fee charged for processing passport applications, as long as they follow the State Department's rules. It would also require the Secretary of State, within 30 days of enactment, to authorize any public library that previously served as a passport acceptance facility and complied with those rules to do so again, and to send Congress a report documenting compliance or explaining any failure to comply. Finally, it would update the Passport Act of 1920 so that public libraries that meet these requirements are listed alongside state and local governments and the Postal Service as entities that can accept passport applications.
